planned.body:
Epic #3443, increment 2: graduates ONE standalone commit from `origin/lane/mechanical-dispatcher` (cherry-picked with `-x`, applied clean, no conflicts).

## What
`1024822db` (#3634) — `scripts/conveyor/reconcile-fix-dispatch.mjs`: the fix-agent scope fence required a resolved backlog item with a declared scope, so PRs delivering an epic (no file-level scope) were silently refused. `planFixesFromReconcile` now falls back to the PR's own already-changed files (new `fetchPrDiffScope`, one `gh pr diff --name-only` call) as the fence. Never looser than a declared scope. A PR whose branch number is a *reviewed* PR (not a delivered item) stays refused; a regression test pins it.

## Behaviour note for review
This changes live fix-dispatch behaviour: one extra `gh pr diff` call when a resolved item has no scope; it fails soft on a `gh` error.

## Verification
- `reconcile-fix-dispatch.test.mjs`: 45/45.
- Plus dependents (reconcile-core/pass/finding, parked-pr-conflict watch + integration, duplicate-pr-watch, all `scripts/operations/__tests__`): 73 files / 2254 tests pass.
- `node scripts/check-standards.mjs`: 0 errors.

## Not in this PR
No lane-pool changes. The prototype branch has no fix for `lane-pool refresh --lane=N` or the busy-lane rule. No watchdog chain (`driver-watchdog.mjs` not on main).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Summary

`clear-stuck-session` (#3383, commit `81d5c9745`) mechanizes the GH #77683 zombie-session workaround — a
`claude agents` entry that stays listed with no live process, where `claude stop`/`claude rm` fail or
silently no-op. This updates every place in the repo that still described the old manual fix (retrying
`claude stop`/`claude rm`, or moving `~/.claude/jobs/<id>/` aside by hand) to point at the operation as the
preferred path, keeping the manual move only as the documented fallback for if the operation itself is
unavailable or fails.

- `agent-memory-src/stuck-claude-sessions-known-issue-workaround.md` — restructured so
  `node scripts/operations/run.mjs clear-stuck-session --session=<id>` (or `--pr=<n>`) is the preferred fix;
  the manual jobs-directory move is now the documented fallback.
- `docs/agent/dispatcher-runbook.md` — "Closing out a stuck `--bg` dispatched agent" now names
  `clear-stuck-session` for a row whose `stop`/`rm` actually fail (the #77683 case), keeping `claude stop` /
  `dispatch-abort.mjs` for a session that just needs stopping (not hitting that bug).
- `scripts/conveyor/reconcile-core.mjs` — the `liveness-unknown` refusal's docblocks (`REFUSAL_KINDS` and
  `assessLiveness`) now point a reader at `clear-stuck-session` for a session confirmed stuck by other means,
  instead of leaving no pointer at all.

**Checked, left unchanged:** `skills-src/mechanical-delivery-doctrine/SKILL.md` — its rule 8 documents a
different, already-fixed bug (`claude stop`/`rm` failing because the full `sessionId` UUID was passed
instead of the short `id`), not this zombie-listing issue, so it doesn't describe the workaround this PR
replaces. `skills-src/conveyor/SKILL.md` already links to `dispatcher-runbook.md` for this exact scenario
(§2, "Operating it, not building it?"), so updating the runbook itself is the one place discoverability
needed to change.

## Test plan

- [x] `node scripts/check-standards.mjs` — 0 errors (pre-existing unrelated warnings only)
- [x] `node scripts/check-memory.mjs` — memory index within budget
- [x] `node scripts/verify-lane.mjs` — green (see run output)

<!-- policy-set: v1 87688229b08c -->

## Summary

`scripts/guard-bash.mjs`'s `reason()` had a false-positive: the `backlog|reports`
append/in-place-edit deny arm (around line 1889) tested `CORPUS_MD` against the
WHOLE raw command string for any `sed`/`tee`/`perl` invocation, so a purely
read-only command that merely *mentioned* a `backlog/`/`reports/` path (e.g.
`sed -n '1,200p' backlog/123-foo.md`, `perl -ne 'print' backlog/123-foo.md`) was
denied with a message about bypassing the locus-prefix write hook — reproduced
live twice in one session on two different files.

The fix reuses `fileWriteTargets(s)` — the same real-write-target extractor
`primaryTreeWriteReason` already calls on this exact segment elsewhere in the
same function — so the check now tests only ACTUAL write targets (a real
`-i`/`--in-place` edit, or a real `tee` write) against `CORPUS_MD`, never the
raw command text. The unrelated `>>`/redirect half of the OR is untouched.

- `scripts/guard-bash.mjs`: swap `atCommand(/^(?:sed|tee|perl)\b/) &&
  CORPUS_MD.test(s)` for `atCommand(/^(?:sed|tee|perl)\b/) &&
  fileWriteTargets(s).some((f) => CORPUS_MD.test(f))`
- `scripts/__tests__/guard-bash.test.mjs`: new describe block
  `sed/tee/perl backlog|reports write vs. mere-mention (#3390)` — negative
  cases (read-only sed/tee/perl mentioning a backlog/reports path must NOT be
  denied) alongside the existing/extended positive cases (a real `-i`/`--in-place`
  edit or `tee` write must still be denied)

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run scripts/__tests__/guard-bash.test.mjs` — 223 tests pass,
      including new negative cases (read-only sed/tee/perl on backlog/reports
      paths allowed) and existing/extended positive cases (real writes still
      denied)
- [x] `npm run check:standards` — 0 errors
- [x] `node scripts/operations/run.mjs verify --checkout=<lane>` — green marker
      recorded for the commit (`npm run test:unit && npm run check:standards`)
